content:
maria (support): FYI escalation from ACME Prod — several end users hit 403 when switching orgs/projects in the console after SSO changes earlier today. Customer says it started around 2024-03-17T09:45Z. Repro steps below.

lina (support): adding screenshots + assertion sample they pasted in DM (redacted).

maria (support): Repro steps we used:
1) Log in via SSO (Okta) -> SAML assertion returned
2) Open /console/orgs -> click project switch for a project user used to have access to
3) 403, UI shows "Permission denied" and no option to request access

maria (support): Key observation from customer: they recently updated Okta transform to shorten group attribute values.

infra-bot: audit.log link: https://log.redwood.internal/orgs/acme/events/2024-03-17T09:46Z (access: support-team)

ben (sre): I tried to replay their SAML (redacted) locally. When assertion has groups payload > ~64 chars the IdP rewrites it to a single truncated value. Our authN header `x-rw-groups` ends up missing expected group names -> downstream RBAC denies.

ben (sre): sample server log snippet:```
2024-03-17T09:46:02Z auth:session validate assertion id=... user=alice@acme.com
2024-03-17T09:46:02Z auth:session headers: x-rw-user=alice@acme.com x-rw-groups=
2024-03-17T09:46:02Z auth:rbac check project:proj-42 result=deny code=403
```

tess (eng): ACK. sounds like Okta attribute transform collapsed the array into a single, truncated string. Our mapping expects `groups[]` or `groups` as CSV; if absent we currently treat as explicit deny. Short-term workaround: ask customer to change IdP to keep full group claim or run a SCIM resync for affected users.

tess (eng): Proposed quick mitigation (internal): on token verification, if `groups` claim is missing but user has a recent SCIM membership entry, fallback to SCIM lookup instead of deny. Will open a conservative PR for fallback logic.

maria (support): Workaround we sent to customer: 1) Toggle "force group sync" in their IdP mapping to expand groups (or revert their transform) OR 2) run our manual resync:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $RENO_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.com/internal/scim/resync?org=acme&users=alice@acme.com"
```
(we flagged that endpoint as dev-only; use with caution, support can run it)

ben (sre): I reproduced project-switch 403 with the truncated claim. After invoking resync, project switch succeeds for that user. Monitoring rule created: `support.sso.403.spike` -> alert to #oncall if >5/min.

tess (eng): I'll draft PR #1224 to add fallback SCIM lookup when groups claim is absent. Behavior: only fallback if token scope includes `scim:read` or internal service token present. ETA EOD.

lina (support): Customer asked for ETA, told them engineering will propose fix today and we can keep using resync as temporary. They asked if this is a recurring risk — we recommended they avoid transforms that truncate claims.

maria (support): tagging final steps: @tess please include a short mitigation doc snippet we can paste to customers. @ben please keep alert on for 24h. :thumbsup:

tess (eng): Will do. I'll include example IdP mapping and a note about CSV vs array mapping.

ben (sre): Monitoring enabled. Closing local repro.

lina (support): Thanks team — I'll update the ticket with workaround + eng ETA and mark escalated -> engineering.

maria (support): Closing internal thread; will reopen if customer sees more failures.
